title: FAMOS: Feed-Forward 3D Articulation Modeling from Sparse Observations
why_read: A technical method for inferring how objects like drawers and hinges move from sparse camera views, relevant to robotics and 3D vision researchers.
analysis: FAMOS is a model that predicts which parts of an object can move and how (joint parameters) from a small set of partial 3D point clouds, rather than requiring dense scans or many views. It uses a transformer architecture that combines information across multiple observations and can even work from a single view when necessary. The authors also built a synthetic data generator to work around the scarcity of labeled articulated-object datasets. This is a fairly specialized computer vision contribution mainly of interest to robotics and 3D reconstruction researchers.
